findings.reason: an implementer following §6 as written would key change detection on pointer+stream alone and silently drop every delivery whose manifest moved on its own; the sentence must name the manifest and the run-directory records as change inputs (or require the classifier's memo key to gate the run directory's real inputs).
findings.text: "The classifier (`recovery.classify_pointer`) runs once per run whose inputs changed" is not produced by the mechanism the section states: §6's change detection (:160–162) watches only the pointer's `file_memo.file_signature` and the stream's stored offset, whereas the classifier's real input set is `recovery_memo._classification_inputs` (reckon/crew/recovery_memo.py:450–472), which also names the manifest, the run directory's records (`_CLASSIFICATION_RUN_RECORDS`), the review-store candidates and the tree head; the pointer's own `phase` "only `observe` advances" (reckon/crew/directory.py:100–101), so a worker that finishes by writing its manifest delivers without touching the pointer or the stream, and the station would never reclassify it — the delivered transition §7 must write once never appears.

findings.reason: without a tick where only the manifest moves, the measure cannot fail for the one input that carries the delivery signal, so §6's gate would certify an incomplete classifier.
findings.text: the three-tick measure moves "one run's pointer or stream" and never a manifest alone, so it passes on an implementation that reclassifies only on pointer/stream movement, which is exactly the defect above; none of its three negative controls (:175–177) exercises a manifest-only change.
